description: Fuse the Base64 decode with downstream error-detection (CRC/checksum) computation in a single SIMD pass, borrowing from the concept of fused decode+ECC in communication receivers. Since many Base64 payloads are immediately checksummed (e.g., in JWT verification, S/MIME), computing the checksum during decode eliminates a second pass over the data.
mathematical_formalization: Let D(x) = Base64 decode of input x, and C(y) = CRC32 of decoded output y. Normally: cost = T_D + T_C (two passes). Fused: as each 48-byte decoded block is produced in a ZMM register, immediately compute CRC32 on it before storing. Using VPCLMULQDQ (carry-less multiply), CRC32 of 64 bytes costs ~8 instructions. Fused cost: T_D + delta (where delta << T_C because data is already in registers).
analogical_connections: Communication receivers: Viterbi decode + CRC check in single pipeline stage
Database: predicate pushdown computes WHERE clause during decompression scan
Image processing: fused debayer + white-balance in a single shader pass
implementation_hypothesis: After the multiply-add packing step produces 48 decoded bytes in a ZMM register, feed those bytes directly into a CRC32 computation using VPCLMULQDQ (or CRC32 instruction for 8 bytes at a time). Maintain a running CRC state across blocks. At the end, compare against expected CRC. This adds ~2-3 instructions per 48-byte block on top of the decode cost.
experiment_seed: Implement fused decode+CRC32 and compare against separate decode then CRC32. Measure total cycles for 1MB input. Expected: fused saves ~40% of the standalone CRC32 cost due to eliminating reload from memory.
